parsed.vignette:
A 57-year-old man presents to the emergency department with several days of malaise, weakness, and night sweats. Today, he experienced a headache with blurry vision, thus prompting his presentation. The patient has a history of diabetes and is followed closely by an endocrinologist. Otherwise, he has lost 10 pounds over the past month. His temperature is 100°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 122/90 mmHg, pulse is 84/min, respirations are 16/min, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air. Physical exam is notable for a thin man but is otherwise unremarkable. His visual acuity is 20/100 in both eyes, though he says that he normally has 20/20 vision. His gait is mildly ataxic as well, but his neurological exam is otherwise nonfocal. Laboratory studies are ordered as seen below.

Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL
Hematocrit: 31%
Leukocyte count: 57,500/mm^3 with 35% blasts
Platelet count: 109,000/mm^3

Serum:
Na+: 139 mEq/L
Cl-: 100 mEq/L
K+: 4.1 Eq/L
HCO3-: 22 mEq/L
BUN: 20 mg/dL
Glucose: 99 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Calcium: 10.0 mEq/L
parsed.question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

branches.label: Myeloid Neoplasm with Increased Blasts
askable_discriminators: Presence of bone pain or splenomegaly
branches.why_included: High blast percentage (35%) and subacute constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss) strongly suggest myeloid blast lineage (AML/CML blast crisis/PV). Requires cytogenetics to differentiate from chronic MPN in advanced phase.

branches.label: Lymphoproliferative / Plasma Cell Disorder
askable_discriminators: Evidence of B-cell chronicity (e.g., lymphocytosis pattern)
branches.why_included: Differential covers broad lymphocyte monoclonality (CLL) and plasma cell proliferation (myeloma). Visual changes suggest potential hyperviscosity syndromes (myeloma), which are urgent to address.

branches.label: Chronic Myeloproliferative Neoplasm (chronic/accelerated phase)
branches.why_included: CML in early phases may show <20% blasts and mild leukocytosis. Requires BCR-ABL testing to separate from de novo AML/CML blast crisis.

branches.label: Reactive / Non-malignant Leukocytosis with Atypical Blasts
askable_discriminators: Clinical clues for leukemoid reaction (e.g., high fever, bacterial cultures pending)
branches.why_included: Low-probability but non-malignant cause (e.g., extreme infection) could mimic blasts. Needs exclusion with infectious/inflammatory testing.

branches.label: Inflammatory/Metabolic Syndrome with Hematologic Mimicry
branches.why_included: Diabetes may indirectly link to atypical presentations (e.g., sepsis with blast transformation). Requires testing to exclude infectious/metabolic causes.
